messages:
chris: Seeing a weird spike in write amplification on a subset of scratch NVMe in us-west2 during a GPU autoscale event. GPU attaches slowed and a few nodes reported I/O checksum warnings.
chris: snippet from node gnode-142: `ata3: nvme0: write_amp: 18x -> 65x, scrub_rate=3, reclaim=8`
chris: dmesg tail: 
```
[03:14:02] nvme0: write amplification detected, rwerr=0x2 crc=1
[03:14:05] nvme0: sector remap triggered, async scrub queued
[03:14:12] nvme0: iops drop -> gpu-attach wait 1200ms
```

maria: ugh. did this coincide with the big batch-provision at 03:10?
alex: yes, autoscaler pushed ~120 GPUs in a 2m window in us-west2, high concurrent scratch creates janitor churn.
chris: believe the pattern is: bursty GPU launches -> many ephemeral writes -> janitor + scrub overlap -> write amplification spikes -> hidden remap/corruption warnings.
jen: @maria @chris any quick mitigations we can flip to reduce attach failures?
maria: I'm already lowering janitor concurrency on us-west2 to 2. also temporarily paused nightly deep-scrub for the zone.
maria: command I ran: `infractl scrub set-concurrency --zone us-west2 --concurrency 2`
kai: can we throttle autoscaler ramp? suggest ramp_rate=30 GPUs/min for next hour to avoid bursts.
alex: I'll add a rollout to the scale policy: `PATCH /autoscaler/policies/us-west2 {"ramp_rate":30}` — doing canary to 5% of requests.
chris: putting read-only healthprobe on suspected nodes and fencing ones that show CRC>0. also opening an incident for storage team.
sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-458 opened by chris for us-west2 nvme write-amplification spike. Pager notified to #incidents.
jen: good. we should also surface SMART attributes and firmware revision for the affected drives — remap rate could be firmware-sensitive.
chris: collected smartctl output and posted to the incident. key lines: `Realloc_Sectors=3, Media_Errors=1, Firmware=3.2.1`
alex: temporary mitigation: routing GPU attach traffic to eu-west1 for latency-tolerant jobs, prescheduling critical jobs to dedicated pool.
maria: note: cost hit expected if we shift region. estimated delta ~+12% for next 3 hours. ops OK with that to preserve SLA.
chris: longer-term: add gentle backpressure in the attach path when local NVMe queue depth > 1500 iops/s per device, and have autoscaler listen to storage pressure signal.
kai: agree. create RFC? I can draft a short proposal for autoscaler-storage handshake.
jen: FYI, firmware team flagged that 3.2.x has a remap regression under sustained small writes; they're pushing 3.2.2 candidate.
chris: for now, action items: 1) throttle autoscaler ramp (alex) 2) reduce janitor/scrub concurrency (maria) 3) fence any nodes with CRC>0 (chris) 4) route noncritical workloads off us-west2 (alex) 5) incident tracking (sre-bot)
alex: patch deployed for ramp_rate canary, removing 5% after observation window if stable.
maria: scrub concurrency lowered. monitoring graphs look better — write_amp metric dropped from 65x -> 22x in 8m.
chris: still seeing a handful of remap warnings on older firmware. tagging devices and scheduling replacement during maintenance window.
jen: Thanks team. Please add any postmortem notes to the incident and link to the autoscaler-storage RFC when available. :triangle_exclamation:
chris: filing follow-up: will upload query to perf metrics for correlation between `scratch_write_ps` and `gpu_attach_latency` over the last 48h.
kai: I'll start the RFC draft and ping infra-arch for review.
chris: closing thread here, moving discussion to INC-2026-458 and rfc/autoscaler-storage-backpressure. thx everyone :thumbsup:
